correctness.rationale: The two fully standalone C++17 exhaustive algorithms independently classify all 2^23 inputs for each graph. One uses precomputed neighbor bitmasks and functional-graph indegree peeling; the other uses per-edge bit tests and individual path detection. They agree exactly on both complete first-entry/period histograms, all primitive cycle counts and basin sizes. Each histogram sums to 8,388,608. Explicit period and sharp-depth witnesses were directly iterated; no finite experiment is substituted for an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Comparing the Paley and circular carousel orientations is naturally motivated: both are canonical, vertex-transitive, degree-11 regular tournaments on the same 23 labelled sites but have distinct local geometries. The exact disjoint four-versus-twenty-three periods and ~56-fold attraction contrast show that degree and vertex-transitivity alone do not describe directed majority attractors. The full state-space basin probabilities and sharp transient ceilings are reusable benchmarks for directed threshold dynamics; these quantities are not generic naming changes or tiny marginal improvements.
